item.title: RIG-I-MAVS-IFN-NOXA axis coordinates antiviral innate response and apoptosis during parahenipavirus infection
item.description: Gamak virus (GAKV) is a recently identified shrew-borne paramyxovirus belonging to the genus Parahenipavirus, which also includes the zoonotic Langya virus (LayV). Despite the growing recognition of shrew-associated paramyxoviruses, the host pathways that detect infection and regulate antiviral responses remain poorly understood. In this study, we characterized host responses to GAKV infection using integrated in vitro and in vivo approaches. GAKV infection induced robust innate immune responses...

item.title: AI-Based Generative Search for New Altermagnetic Candidates With Large Spin Splitting
item.description: Altermagnets combine zero net magnetization with momentum-dependent spin splitting, yet materials exhibiting sizable spin splitting remain scarce. Herein, a high-throughput discovery workflow is presented that integrates diffusion-based crystal generation with targeted screening and first-principles validation to identify new altermagnet candidates beyond existing databases. Starting from 51 200 generated structures, candidates are downselected using an artificial intelligence-based classifier,...

item.title: Spinal dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate induces convulsion-like behavior via NMDA receptor-mediated Ca<sup>2+</sup> influx and sigma-1 receptor-mediated intracellular Ca<sup>2+</sup> release
item.description: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS) is a neurosteroid that modulates spinal nociception and hyperalgesia. However, the immediate impact of an acute increase in spinal DHEAS remains poorly understood. Here, we report that intrathecal (i.t.) administration of DHEAS (0.3-10 nmol) dose-dependently induces an abrupt, transient convulsion-like behavior lasting approximately 5 min in mice, whereas its unconjugated form DHEA exhibits no such effect. This behavior was significantly attenuated by...

item.title: Metabolic reprogramming of the acetogen Clostridium sp. AWRP via adaptive laboratory evolution for improved formate-based growth
item.description: Formate is a promising, sustainable feedstock for microbial conversion into value-added products via the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway. Based on the identification of three distinct formate dehydrogenases in Clostridium sp. AWRP, this study investigated the potential of this acetogen for formate-based growth. Although the wild-type strain exhibited an extended lag phase due to formate toxicity, adaptive laboratory evolution yielded the adapted strain F30T, which demonstrated a significantly enhanced...

item.title: Heterogeneous TRAb trajectories after total thyroidectomy in graves' disease with thyroid eye disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: Postoperative TRAb levels generally declined but followed heterogeneous trajectories that may reflect persistent systemic TSH receptor autoimmunity; however, these trajectories appear to have limited utility for predicting ophthalmic outcomes in patients with predominantly longstanding, low-activity TED.

item.title: Dance Charisma and fan identity in live concerts: a serial-mediation model of kinesthetic empathy, perceived emotional synchrony, and collective effervescence
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Live concerts continue to thrive in an age of digital saturation, suggesting that bodily co-presence resists virtual substitution. We ask how dance charisma relates to a theoretically specified sequence culminating in fan identity. Integrating mirror-neuron theory, emotional contagion, neo-Durkheimian theory, and social identity theory, we propose a serial-mediation model relating dance charisma to social identity through kinesthetic empathy, perceived emotional synchrony, and...

item.title: On-device reinforcement learning-based insulin dosing controller for fully automated insulin delivery
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems integrate continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with algorithm-driven insulin dosing to enable closed-loop glycemic management for people with type 1 diabetes (T1D). Recent advances in wearable glucose sensing and insulin delivery technologies have enabled increasingly compact AID systems; however, deploying advanced AI-based dosing algorithms directly on resource-constrained wearable devices remains technically challenging. Some AID...

item.title: Fully biocatalytic stereodivergent conversion of levulinic acid to enantiopure γ-valerolactone
item.description: γ-Valerolactone (GVL) is a biomass-derived platform chemical with broad industrial applications, while its enantiopure forms are valuable chiral building blocks for fine-chemical synthesis. Here, we developed a fully biocatalytic Escherichia coli whole-cell cascade for the stereodivergent conversion of levulinic acid (LA) to enantiopure (R)- or (S)-GVL. The modular system integrates stereocomplementary LA reduction by engineered dehydrogenases, formate dehydrogenase (FDH)-dependent nicotinamide...

item.title: The psychological dynamics of AI in education: how bright traits and dark apprehensions relate to perceived academic performance and continuance
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in higher education, yet the psychological factors associated with students' continued use remain unclear. Integrating the Expectation-Confirmation Model, Two-Factor Theory, and Cognitive Appraisal Theory, this study examines how perseverance of effort, consistency of interest, technophobia, and creepiness relate to cognitive evaluations, perceived AI-assisted academic performance, and continuance intention. Survey data from 655...

item.title: Establishment of Korean National Diagnostic Reference Levels for Fluoroscopy in 2025
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Compared with the 2021 DRLs, the updated DAP-based DRLs showed heterogeneous change patterns across examination types. These differences may be attributable to multiple factors, including variations in clinical protocols, equipment settings, and the composition of participating institutions. The limited participation of smaller hospitals and clinics should also be considered when interpreting the DRLs for certain examinations. Continued education, promotion of DRL utilization, and...

item.title: Characterisation of the Novel HLA-B*35:652 Allele Identified by Next-Generation Sequencing
item.description: HLA-B*35:652 differs from HLA-B*35:01:01:01 by single nonsynonymous nucleotide change in Exon 2 position 148 G>C.

item.title: Identification of Potential Biomarkers for Early Detection of Breast Cancer Based on Plasma Proteomics
item.description: Breast cancer (BC) is one of the most commonly diagnosed malignancies among women worldwide. However, current diagnostic methods, including imaging techniques and serum tumor markers such as CA15-3 and CEA, lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity for early detection. To identify novel blood-based biomarkers for BC, we performed a proteomic analysis using plasma samples from BC patients. Quantitative analysis based on DIA-MS revealed that among proteasome-related proteins, proteasome subunit...

item.title: Nine-Year Longitudinal Changes in Salivary Gland Ultrasonography in Primary Sjögren's Disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: SGUS abnormalities progressed over long-term follow-up in primary SjD, and higher baseline SGUS burden was associated with subsequent progression.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence for Bone Health Assessment in Hand and Wrist Radiographs: A Systematic Review
item.description: Background: Hand and distal radius fractures are increasingly recognised as sentinel events that may precede more serious osteoporotic fractures of the hip and spine. Despite growing awareness of osteoporosis assessment after fragility fractures, adoption into clinical practice has remained inadequate. As frontline providers managing sentinel fractures, hand surgeons are optimally positioned to identify compromised bone health. Because hand and wrist radiographs are routinely obtained in...

item.title: Physical Artificial Intelligence in Surgery: Current Status and Future Perspectives for Hand Surgery
item.description: Surgical procedures follow a cycle of perception, decision-making and physical execution. While artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly helped with sensing and decision-making, physical execution still relies on the surgeon's manual skills. Robotic systems such as the da Vinci, Symani and MUSA use a master-slave model, copying the surgeon's movements in real time but lacking independent perception or decision-making. As a result, they are not considered physical AI. Recently, physical...

item.title: Surgeon-Performed Ultrasonography in Hand Surgery: Beyond Diagnosis
item.description: Ultrasonography has become a practical extension of the hand surgeon's clinical examination, and its value now reaches well beyond diagnosis. Performed by the operating surgeon, high-resolution ultrasound provides real-time, dynamic, point-of-care information that can be obtained in the actual surgical position and compared side to side with the contralateral hand, functioning in effect as a surgical navigation system. This review illustrates, through a series of selected operative cases, how...

item.title: Linking Cognitive Frailty to Suicidal Ideation in Visually Impaired Older Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study
item.description: Older adults with visual impairment are vulnerable to suicidal ideation, likely due to the interplay between physical decline, cognitive impairment and psychosocial challenges. Cognitive frailty, defined as the coexistence of physical frailty and mild cognitive impairment, has emerged as a multidimensional construct; however, its relevance to suicidal ideation in this population has not been sufficiently investigated. This study investigated the association between cognitive frailty and suicidal...

item.title: Defining the problem of pandemic resource allocation: perspectives from healthcare providers and civil society advocates in South Korea
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Pandemic resource allocation was shaped by differing understandings of what counted as a resource, who qualified as a legitimate subject of allocation, and what outcomes counted as survival. Equitable preparedness requires ethical principles, equity safeguards, and participatory governance to be institutionalized before a public health emergency occurs.

item.title: Establishment and tenogenic characterization of canine tendon-derived stem cells compared with adipose-derived stem cells
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study established cTDSCs as a tendon-specific mesenchymal stem cell population with superior tenogenic responsiveness to cADSCs. These findings provide foundational, species-specific data for future translational research on canine tendon repair and regenerative therapies.

item.title: Impact of rehabilitation-focused physician follow-up on activities of daily living 6 months after discharge from convalescent rehabilitation wards: a retrospective cohort study
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Physician involvement after discharge from convalescent rehabilitation wards is inconsistent in Japan. While the value of board-certified physiatrists during inpatient rehabilitation is established, the impact of rehabilitation-focused physicians on long-term outcomes remains unclear. This study examined the association between regular postdischarge examinations by rehabilitation-focused physicians and activities of daily living (ADL) 6 months after discharge.

item.title: Reaction of the AGE precursor glycolaldehyde with deoxynucleosides and its detection in foods
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest that, in addition to endogenous and environmental GA, dietary GA may also affect physiological AGE levels or induce DNA damage and enhance the risk of various diseases, including cancer.

item.title: Suspected retention of magnesium oxide tablets during co-administration with recovery K5, a concentrated oral enteral nutrition formula, supported by in vitro disintegration testing
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This brief report does not establish definitive causality, but it identifies a clinically relevant signal supported by in vitro evidence. These findings support pharmacist-led review of the actual administration sequence, water volume, and dosage-form selection when MgO tablets are administered concomitantly with Recovery K5, a concentrated oral EN formula.

item.title: Development of [<sup>131</sup>I]-Labeled Hesperidin for Potential Breast Cancer Theranostic Applications: Computational, Radiochemical, and Biological Evaluation
item.description: CONCLUSION: [^(131)I]-hesperidin demonstrated favorable computational, radiochemical, and cellular characteristics, supporting its further investigation as a potential breast cancer theranostic radiopharmaceutical candidate. The stable molecular interactions, acceptable short-term radiochemical stability, enhanced cellular uptake relative to free iodine-131, and increased ROS generation collectively indicate its potential for targeted radiopharmaceutical applications. Further preclinical studies...

item.title: Associations of Weight-Bearing Lunge Test Performance and Occiput-to-Wall Distance With Chronic Low Back Pain Intensity in Older Adults
item.description: CONCLUSION: In older adults with chronic LBP, lower WBLT performance remained significantly associated with greater pain intensity in the fully adjusted model, whereas the association between OWD and pain intensity was not statistically significant. However, OWD showed higher discriminatory ability in the exploratory ROC analysis and was significantly associated with pain intensity in an additional sensitivity analysis. Both measures may provide complementary clinical information, although the...

item.title: Early-Childhood Insurance Gaps and Preventive Care Outcomes Among Young Children in a Low-Barrier Pediatric Mobile Clinic in Washington, D.C
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This population demonstrated a high prevalence of EIG during a critical developmental period. EIG were not associated with reduced WCV attendance or vaccination completion, which may reflect the clinic's low-barrier, comprehensive care model. These findings highlight limitations of existing cross-sectional insurance metrics in capturing early childhood coverage gaps and suggest tailored care models warrant further study as a strategy for supporting preventive care equity in...

item.title: Microglial lipid handling in white matter aging: mechanistic evidence, context dependence, and implications for repair
item.description: White matter aging increases the supply of cholesterol-rich myelin debris while reducing the capacity for tissue repair. Demyelination experiments show that phagocytes can engulf myelin yet retain cholesteryl esters when lysosomal processing or cholesterol efflux is inadequate. Lipid droplets can buffer acute lipid stress, but persistent droplets can accompany impaired turnover, oxidative injury, and defective remyelination. This Review evaluates evidence across uptake, storage, lysosomal...

item.title: Research outputs of African national public health agencies on emergency preparedness and response: scoping review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: As measured by scientific publications in the public domain and meeting inclusion criteria, NPHAs in the WHO African Region demonstrated an ability to generate and disseminate scientific evidence during periods of acute public health need. Most publications were associated with a small number of NPHAs and a small number of public health topics; the rate of new publications across the region's NPHAs declined following the COVID-19 pandemic. Scientific publication represents only one...

item.title: Radiation Therapy for Adult Head and Neck Sarcomas: A Systematic Review With Emerging Perspectives on Particle Therapy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Radiation therapy remains a cornerstone of multidisciplinary management of adult head and neck sarcomas. Clinical evidence for particle therapy remains preliminary, with encouraging outcomes reported for carbon ion radiation therapy but insufficient proton-specific data to draw conclusions. Prospective, collaborative, histology-driven, and biologically informed studies are needed to better define the role of particle therapy and optimize radiation therapy strategies.

item.title: Ethyl caffeate restores BNIP3L-dependent mitophagy and mitochondrial function to ameliorate influenza A virus-induced lung injury
item.description: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection induces severe lung injury characterized by excessive inflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction, in which impaired mitochondrial clearance plays a crucial role. Ethyl caffeate (EC), a bioactive phenolic compound of dietary origin, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. However, its protective role against IAV-triggered lung damage and mitochondrial quality control dysfunction remains poorly defined. In this study, PR8-induced IAV...

item.title: Adaptive immunotherapy dosing in cancer: a structured narrative review and conceptual framework for future clinical investigation
item.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer treatment, but approved schedules do not establish whether treatment intensity should remain constant as tumor burden, immunity, toxicity, and response evolve. Continued treatment after durable response may add toxicity and treatment burden while providing uncertain incremental benefit. This structured narrative review examines adaptive immunotherapy dosing: prespecified, state-dependent modification of dose, interval, or duration,...

item.title: A pulmonary air leak model for integrated assessment of pulmonary sealant performance and tissue remodeling
item.description: Pulmonary sealants are used to manage air leakage after lung surgery. Their preclinical assessment requires a defined pulmonary defect and evaluation of both immediate sealing and subsequent tissue responses. This study examined the effect of defect size on airway pressure in a rat pulmonary air leak model and assessed the application of the selected condition to pulmonary sealant evaluation. Small (2-4 mm) and large (8-10 mm) pulmonary parenchymal defects were created in the right middle lobe...

item.title: Longitudinal frailty trajectories among community-dwelling older adults in Nanjing, China: evidence from routine annual health examinations
item.description: CONCLUSION: Frailty states changed in both directions across annual examinations, while long-term frailty burden showed substantial population heterogeneity. Routine annual health examination data may provide a practical basis for continuous frailty monitoring, identification of priority populations, and stratified health management in community settings.

item.title: Discordance between clinician-rated and patient-reported outcomes during 48-week community care for schizophrenia: longitudinal patterns and associations with insight
item.description: CONCLUSION: During routine community care, patient-reported quality of life improved more than clinician-rated psychopathology and social functioning, with the discrepancy larger and more robust for functioning. Parallel monitoring may better characterize symptom, function, and quality-of-life trajectories, while the role of time-varying insight and treatment attitudes warrants further study.

item.title: Pericapsular Nerve Group Blocks Reduce Immediate Postoperative Opioid Consumption Among Patients Undergoing Anterior Total Hip Arthroplasty but Not Posterior Total Hip Arthroplasty
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PENG blocks significantly reduced PACU opioid consumption in anterior THA but not posterior THA. These findings support the use of PENG blocks in anterior THA, particularly in the outpatient setting, to reduce postoperative opioid use and facilitate early recovery.

item.title: A Modular Analysis of National CHW Curricula from Select Countries in Sub-Saharan Africa
item.description: In response to the compelling evidence on Community Health Worker (CHW) contributions to PHC and UHC, in the past decade, governments across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) have intensified efforts to institute/enhance national CHW training programs to equip this workforce with required competencies. However, minimal published evidence is available on the components of national CHW curricula. The study comprised of an initial descriptive analysis of fifteen national CHW curricula, followed by a...

item.title: Design, synthesis, and antiseizure evaluation of benzhydryl 5-arylfuran-2-carboxylates: GABA-A/SV2A targeting, EEG, and ADMET profiling
item.description: Epilepsy is a persistent neurological disorder marked by recurrent, unprovoked seizures and remains a major worldwide healthcare challenge owing to its profound clinical, cognitive, and psychosocial consequences. This research aimed to design and synthesize a novel series of benzhydryl 5-arylfuran-2-carboxylates via Suzuki cross-coupling (5a-5i), affording good to excellent yields (74-96%), and to evaluate antiseizure potential using acute PTZ-induced seizure and 6 Hz psychomotor seizure models....

item.title: Protecting dignity in serious illness during crises: A public health priority
item.description: Dignity encompasses both the inherent worth of every person and the recognition and protection of that worth through interpersonal, professional, community, and structural conditions. Though dignity frameworks developed primarily in high-income settings lay a foundational ground, they may require contextual adaptation to account for the structural threats to dignity created or intensified by conflict, displacement, resource scarcity, and health-system disruptions. In low- and middle-income...

item.title: From interoperable data to continuous care: a responsive implementation approach to personal health data spaces
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Internet use for learning and insomnia symptoms among high school and university students in China: a two-wave network analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Internet-use activities showed different cross-sectional associations and longitudinal associations at item level with insomnia symptoms. Future research should consider activity type and educational context when studying student internet use and insomnia.

item.title: Feasibility and safety of dual-wavelength 980/1470 nm laser for laparoscopic fenestration of hepatic cysts: a preliminary clinical study
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this small pilot cohort, 980/1470 nm dual-wavelength laser laparoscopic fenestration and drainage appeared feasible and safe, with no severe perioperative complications and favorable short-term imaging outcomes; the single-port application described here represents a single illustrative case. Given the small sample size, absence of a comparator group, and short follow-up, these findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger controlled studies with longer-term...

item.title: Governing genomic AI in the era of agentic systems
item.description: Genomic artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from task-specific models toward systems that can integrate genomic, molecular, and phenotypic information across increasingly complex analytical workflows. There are governance frameworks for the responsible use of genomic AI, largely developed for systems whose data use and analytical behavior are defined in advance. Agentic systems add a new governance challenge because analytical decisions, resource use, and subsequent actions may no longer be...

item.title: Efficacy and safety of Zhichuanling oral liquid in patients with stable asthma-COPD overlap: protocol for a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
item.description: BACKGROUND: Asthma-COPD overlap (ACO) is a heterogeneous chronic airway condition with features of both asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Compared with either disease alone, ACO is usually associated with heavier symptoms, more exacerbations, faster lung-function decline, and poorer quality of life. Stable ACO is typically managed with inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) plus long-acting beta2-agonists (LABA) and/or long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMA), yet many patients...

item.title: Differential early humoral immune response in Lyme disease patients with chronic sequelae
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS) is a chronic illness that lacks validated biomarkers and is thought to be associated with the development of autoimmunity after the initial acute infection. High patient heterogeneity and potentially broad alterations in immune response in PTLDS represent a fundamental challenge and highlight the need for wide and unbiased interrogation of the immune response. High-dimensional antibody-binding platforms can pro le host humoral response...

item.title: Clinical and Research Implications of a Cochrane Systematic Review of Probiotics for Management of Functional Abdominal Pain Disorders in Children
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Bayesian reappraisal of favorable anti-amyloid trials in Alzheimer's disease: updating the cumulative evidence
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Recent favorable trials of anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies have renewed interest in disease-modifying therapies for Alzheimer's disease. However, statistically significant findings from individual trials do not necessarily establish clinically meaningful benefit when interpreted in the context of the existing body of evidence. A cumulative assessment is therefore needed to distinguish evidence for a measurable treatment effect from evidence that its magnitude is clinically...

item.title: Association between vitamin D and lipid profiles in a large Chinese cohort of middle-aged to elderly Chinese men and women: the evidence from China precision nutrition and health- KAP real world study (CPNAS)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: VD showed negatively correlated with dyslipidemia in the general population.

item.title: Business Practices as Implementation Strategies: Using Nudges to Increase Patient Uptake of Complementary and Integrative Health Therapies in the Veterans Health Administration
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Some nudge types and ERIC implementation strategies were used more frequently for encouraging CIH uptake. Gateway, which aligns with the ERIC strategy categories of Train and Educate Stakeholders and Engage Consumers, appears effective at increasing uptake. These findings provide healthcare leaders and practitioners with next steps for improving CIH uptake at their facilities.

item.title: Exploratory immune signatures associated with exercise in pediatric solid tumors
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that the exercise intervention was not associated with broad changes in circulating immune composition in pediatric cancer patients but may instead have been associated with changes in the relative proportions of specific immune populations and/or their distribution within the circulation. Exploratory analyses identified three exercise-associated immune signatures that warrant confirmation in larger, adequately powered studies.

item.title: Cavin-4 peptide immunization induces autoimmunity with features of immune-mediated rippling muscle disease
item.description: Cavin-4 has recently been identified as a target autoantigen in immune-mediated rippling muscle disease (iRMD); however, direct in vivo evidence linking cavin-4 directed immunity to muscle dysfunction is lacking. We therefore evaluated whether cavin-4 peptide immunization could induce cavin-4-directed autoimmunity and generate immunologic and muscle-related features associated with iRMD in mice. Wild-type C57BL/6 mice were immunized with mouse or human cavin-4 peptides (n=10/group); age-matched,...

item.title: Diverging temporal trends and associated factors of adverse birth outcomes among neonates in Guiping, China, 2016-2025: a retrospective study
item.description: CONCLUSION: PTB, LBW, macrosomia, and SGA followed different temporal patterns between 2016 and 2025. SGA decreased, while LBW and macrosomia showed no significant overall changes. PTB declined early in the study period but increased during 2023-2025 in the primary Joinpoint analysis, although this later increase was not statistically significant when uncorrelated errors were assumed. Further research is needed to assess whether the recent increase in PTB continues.

item.title: In vitro characterization and in vivo technical feasibility of biphasic GelMA/HAMA/hydroxyapatite cell-laden hydrogels for osteochondral regeneration: a pilot study in an ovine model
item.description: CONCLUSION: Available in vitro evidence supported the selection of H1 and H3 as candidate chondral and subchondral formulations on the basis of qualitative differentiation profiles. This pilot study supports the technical feasibility of sequential in situ delivery and photopolymerization of these GelMA/HAMA biphasic hydrogels loaded with WJ-MSCs in a large-animal model and provides preliminary descriptive data useful for designing larger, adequately powered confirmatory studies.

item.title: Mechanically stable, endothelializable vascular graft scaffolds fabricated by melt electrowriting
item.description: Conventional synthetic vascular grafts, especially for small-diameter vessels (<6 mm), still face critical limitations in clinical settings, as around 75% of synthetic conduits fail within 3 years of implantation mostly due to the missing luminal endothelial cell layer, leading to, e.g., thrombosis, calcification, and intimal hyperplasia. Mechanical mismatch between the graft and native tissue can lead to severe clinical complications. Thus, tissue-engineered vascular grafts have become of wide...

item.title: Editorial: Lymphocytes and autoimmune disease: from molecular mechanism to clinical implications
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Ingredient-absence and non-addition claims in Chinese online grocery listings: a pre-implementation baseline for the 2027 labeling standards
item.description: CONCLUSION: By retaining unevaluable listings, this audit reports policy-relevant wording and the evidence available to assess it within the same retail frame. The dated baseline supports interpretation of subsequent monitoring across the 2027 transition. Its estimates concern the audited listings and evidence protocol, rather than whole-interface visibility or legal compliance.

item.title: Early detection of drug-resistant epilepsy via multi-domain EEG fusion with prefrontal candidate biomarkers
item.description: Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) is associated with poor clinical outcomes. Interictal scalp EEG-based DRE identification faces a methodological limitation: segment-level models often capture individual-specific EEG patterns rather than group-level pathological differences. In this retrospective study of 42 patients (21 DRE, 21 non-DRE), we constructed an EEG-based DRE recognition framework. Multi-domain features (temporal, spectral, nonlinear) were extracted, and a mutual validation strategy...

item.title: Comparative structural engineering of Euglena phytoene synthase reveals functional residues in carotenoid biosynthesis
item.description: Carotenoids are high-value natural pigments providing antioxidant benefits in healthcare and various industries. Phytoene synthase (PSY/CrtB), which catalyzes the first committed step in carotenoid biosynthesis, is a key determinant of metabolic flux and a major target for enzyme engineering. Although functional amino acid substitutions have been extensively characterized in plant PSYs, it remains unclear whether these structure-function relationships are conserved across evolutionarily distant...

item.title: Relationship Between Sedentary Behavior and Mode of Commuting Among Physical Therapy Students in Okayama Prefecture, Japan
item.description: Introduction The duration of sedentary behavior is closely linked to various health outcomes. The sedentary behavior of physical therapy students is suspected to increase due to their classes and other commitments. Commuting to university is considered to have a significant impact on sedentary behavior in daily life. Therefore, the present study investigated the relationship between sedentary behavior and mode of commuting among physical therapy students in Okayama Prefecture, Japan. Methods A...

item.title: Hallucinating Together: AI Chatbots in Psychedelic Therapy
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Chess-based cognitive remediation training and alcohol cue reactivity in alcohol use disorder: exploratory evidence for supplementary motor area activation changes
item.description: CONCLUSION: These exploratory findings indicate differential longitudinal SMA activation between groups during alcohol-cue viewing relative to rest. CB-CRT might have additional effect against depressive symptoms, though this finding was affected by baseline severity and requires further validation.

item.title: A Survey of Interpretation and Translation Systems for Infectious Disease Response Involving Foreign Residents in the Gyeongnam Region in 2025
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Language support in the Gyeongnam Region currently depends on institution-specific resources, with limited availability of standardized materials and specialized training. Multilingual investigation forms, standardized manuals and glossaries, professional training programs, and coordinated local networks may improve the accuracy of infectious disease response among foreign populations.

item.title: Detection of candidate acoustic biomarkers for Parkinson's disease using an explainable machine learning composite spectrogram approach
item.description: CONCLUSION: The proposed explainable composite spectrogram approach enabled identification of a candidate vowel-level biomarker while retaining high classification performance. Concordance between ML and acoustic analyses suggests the potential of explainable ML in PD speech assessment, pending validation in larger cohorts and other languages.

item.title: Case Report: Postoperative central nervous system infections caused by carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
item.description: Sulbactam-durlobactam in combination with a carbapenem is recommended as the preferred treatment for invasive carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) infections in the 2026 Infectious Diseases Society of America guidance. However, clinical experience with sulbactam-durlobactam for treating CRAB-induced central nervous system (CNS) infections remains extremely limited, and intraventricular/intrathecal polymyxins are still recommended as established therapy for CRAB...

item.title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in serum and tap water of Latina women in a California agricultural community: a CHAMACOS pilot study
item.description: Few studies have characterized per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) exposure in U.S. agricultural communities, despite plausible occupational and environmental sources. In this pilot study within the CHAMACOS cohort (Salinas Valley, California), we measured 42 PFAS in serum (2022-2023) from 20 women (primarily Mexican-born; median age ~49 years) and 48 PFAS in their home tap water (July 2023) and administered a water-use and diet questionnaire. Most women (80%) mainly drank bottled or...

item.title: Serial serum biomarkers at 72 h are associated with subsequent brain death/death by neurologic criteria after acute brain injury
item.description: CONCLUSION: Serial NSE and S100B showed stronger discrimination at 72 h than initially but did not outperform concurrent neurological examination. The short interval to BD/DNC and frequent pupillary non-reactivity indicate that 72-h values may often reflect already advanced injury; these findings support a complementary role within multimodal neuroprognostication rather than prediction of a temporally remote event.

item.title: Preoperative Prediction of Hypoxia Status in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Using Gadoxetic Acid-Enhanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Hypoxia was associated with immune suppression in HCC. The combined intra-peritumoral radiomic model predicted tumor hypoxia more accurately than the conventional MRI feature model and may help guide therapeutic stratification.

item.title: An in-materia neural-network hardware accelerator
item.description: Deep neural networks (DNNs) require extensive computational operations and large amounts of training data to achieve robust performance in applications such as computer vision and natural language processing. Hardware acceleration has become a standard approach to reduce processing latency and energy consumption in DNN deployment, particularly in resource-constrained edge environments. However, current digital technologies are struggling to meet the computational demands, posing significant...

item.title: Promoting older adults' wellbeing in meaningful intergenerational learning contexts
item.description: The mechanisms through which intergenerational learning promotes older adults' wellbeing can be examined through several interrelated dimensions. First, sustained and meaningful intergenerational interactions can strengthen older adults' social connectedness and sense of belonging, alleviate feelings of social isolation, and encourage their participation in community activities and social life. Second, when older adults have opportunities to share their life wisdom, traditional skills, and...

item.title: Comparative and longitudinal assessment of shear-wave elastography in subacute thyroiditis: classical versus clinically atypical subacute thyroiditis phenotypes
item.description: CONCLUSION: Thyroid stiffness was markedly increased at diagnosis in both phenotypes and decreased during follow-up. The between-group differences narrowed at later visits, although their clinical importance remains uncertain. Serial SWE documented changes in thyroid stiffness during SAT resolution, but its added value beyond clinical, laboratory, and conventional ultrasound assessment remains to be established.

item.title: Stress Hyperglycemia Predicts Recurrent Stroke in Patients With Acute Mild Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA of Presumed Atherosclerotic Cause
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this post hoc analysis, stress hyperglycemia was significantly associated with increased risks of recurrent stroke among Chinese patients with acute mild IS or high-risk TIA of presumed atherosclerotic cause. Further investigation is needed to validate this association and explore the underlying mechanisms.

item.title: No detectable choroid plexus enlargement in clinically premanifest Huntington's disease
item.description: BackgroundHuntington's disease (HD) is a progressive autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by an expanded CAG repeat in the HTT gene, producing an elongated polyglutamine tract in the huntingtin protein. The disease is characterized by motor dysfunction, cognitive decline, and psychiatric symptoms, with early striatal neurodegeneration. HD is also associated with immune activation and neuroinflammation. The choroid plexus (ChP), a vascularized structure responsible for...

item.title: TORCH-panel IgM seropositivity and complete hearing recovery in sudden sensorineural hearing loss
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND SIGNIFICANCE: In this selected retrospective cohort, TORCH-panel IgM seropositivity was independently associated with a lower likelihood of complete hearing recovery, whereas no statistically significant association was observed with 3-month PTA. These exploratory findings warrant prospective validation.

item.title: The effect of cognitive load on neural responses to sweet and sour tastes
item.description: ABSTRACTDistracted consumption, or eating while multitasking, is increasingly common and has been linked to overconsumption. Prior research suggests that high cognitive load, due to multitasking, interferes with taste perception and preference, and alters neural activation and connectivity in taste-related and reward-related brain areas. Yet, the exact interplay between the neural mechanisms underlying sensory and hedonic processing of taste under cognitive load remains to be assessed. In a...

item.title: Analysis of lesions in lumbar spine MRI in professionally active soldiers in screening tests
item.description: BackgroundThe work of a soldier is associated with many factors that may be harmful to the body and occur both during military missions and during preparation for them.PurposeTo perform a comprehensive analysis of the lumbar spine condition in professional soldiers based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).Material and MethodsIn total, 70 controls and 66 soldiers who have been in active professional duty on military missions for at least 10 years were examined. A comprehensive analysis of...

item.title: Mapping Invasiveness in Metastatic Spinal Tumor Surgery: A Scoping Review of Operative Surrogates
item.description: Study DesignScoping Review.ObjectiveTo identify operative variables and associated clinical outcomes reported in metastatic spinal tumor surgery (MSTS) that may inform the characterization of surgical invasiveness.MethodsA literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE covered January 1, 2009 to February 29, 2024. The search included terms related to operative variables, complications, and outcomes. Descriptive statistics and a narrative synthesis summarized operative characteristics, perioperative...

item.title: Perioperative Nerve Blockade for Acute Postoperative Pain Management After Major Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
item.description: The efficacy of nerve blockade for perioperative pain management in oral and maxillofacial surgery remains inadequately explored. This study investigated whether perioperative nerve blockade reduces acute postoperative pain (POP) following oral and maxillofacial surgery. Medical records of patients who underwent oral and maxillofacial surgery were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were classified into the "block group" (nerve blockade for major surgery: surgical field diameter ≥ 3 cm, procedure...

item.title: A Nano-Engineered Intelligent Hydrogel Scaffold Hierarchically Regulates Microenvironment for Cranial Bone Regeneration
item.description: Elevated levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and a severely imbalanced immune microenvironment in cranial bone defects not only suppress the osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) but also exacerbate cellular senescence, severely impairing the bone regeneration process. Establishing early immunomodulation and anti-senescence protection is crucial for enhancing cranial defect repair. This study designed a spatiotemporally responsive hierarchically regulates...

item.title: Host and Environmental Determinants of Rodent-Borne Pathogen Infection at Land Border Ports in Xinjiang, China: A GLMM-Based Exploratory Study
item.description: Xinjiang's land border ports are key Eurasian transport nodes where wildlife, domestic animals, and freight traffic converge, creating potential interfaces for transboundary spread of rodent-borne zoonotic pathogens. However, systematic surveillance integrating multiple rodent hosts, diverse pathogens, and environmental drivers across these ports remains limited, limiting our ability to prioritize surveillance and assess transboundary risks. This study screened 869 rodents across 20 species from...

item.title: Oral microorganism-mediated immune responses: implications for inflammatory bowel disease
item.description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, nonspecific inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract. Oral microorganisms have emerged as important contributors to the progression of IBD, and the immune responses triggered by these microorganisms appear to represent a core pathogenic mechanism. In this review, we integrate evidence from clinical and experimental studies demonstrating oral microbiome dysbiosis and the ectopic colonization of oral microorganisms in the intestine in IBD....

item.title: Sex-based differences in Veterans Affairs hospital admissions across rural and urban facilities: A descriptive database analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Despite being a decade younger than men, women veterans have similar hospitalization characteristics. As the population ages, VHA inpatient facilities can expect more admissions from women veterans. High rates of past sexual trauma and mental health comorbidity may require sex-specific differences in service provision.

item.title: Polymorph-Dependent Morphological Diversity in Melt-Stretched Poly(vinylidene fluoride) Revealed by In Situ Synchrotron X-ray Scattering
item.description: Applying flow fields can effectively regulate the polymorphic crystallization of poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) melts, yet the detailed phase structures and morphological evolution remain largely unexplored. Herein, flow-induced polymorphism and lamellar packing modes were systematically investigated using in situ synchrotron wide-angle X-ray diffraction (WAXD) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). Polymorph formation was demonstrated to respond strongly to flow strength: the polar γ- and...

item.title: Developing an Application in Hand Surgery Using Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Applications (App) using artificial intelligence (AI) may change how hand surgery is delivered, particularly through smartphones, portable imaging, wearable sensors and generative AI. This review summarises current evidence on AI App relevant to hand surgery app development, including imaging-based diagnosis, non-imaging diagnosis, functional assessment, rehabilitation, prognostic prediction, large language models (LLMs), commercialisation and regulation. Imaging AI for fracture detection is...

item.title: Effects of Establishing Residency Training Sites on Primary Care Physician Supply in Nonmetropolitan Counties: Evidence From 2010 to 2021
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Establishing residency training sites in nonmetropolitan counties expands county-level PCP supply. The delayed, compounding impact suggests the need for sustained, long-term investment when evaluating the outcomes of the rural residency programs. Heterogeneous effects across geography, population, economic conditions, and healthcare infrastructure signal that stakeholders should consider these contextual factors while expanding rural residency programs.

item.title: Spatially Organized Core-Shell Microcapsules Harness Epidermal-Dermal Coupling for Anti-Photoaging Therapy
item.description: Skin aging involves concurrent epidermal barrier dysfunction and dermal metabolic decline, yet current interventions largely neglect functional coupling between these layers. Herein, a core-shell microcapsule system (SA@B@Lips) is designed for spatially organized and sustained delivery. Specifically, SA@B@Lips supports prolonged probiotic confinement under the tested in vitro conditions, while Dil-associated fluorescence indicates the deeper skin penetration of NMN-loaded liposomes....

item.title: Response: Pregnancy- and lactation-associated osteoporosis: A position statement of the IAPM, IOF, ECTS, ESCEO, IMS, and EMAS
item.description: No abstract

item.title: A double-strand breaks complexity weighted approach for estimating the relative biological effectiveness of carbon ion beams
item.description: CONCLUSION: The DSB complexity-weighted method showed good robustness across a wide LET range human salivary gland tumor (HSG) cells and high precision in describing the RBE of carbon ion beams. It was demonstrated that cell lethality was strongly correlated with the quantity and complexity of DSBs.

item.title: Intraindividual Fluctuations of Neurofilament Light Chain in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: Implications for Repeated Measurements
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) is increasingly used for prognostication, trial stratification, and pharmacodynamic monitoring in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). We sought to quantify intraindividual serum NfL fluctuation, estimate individual base NfL levels, and evaluate prediction intervals for distinguishing natural fluctuation from treatment-related change.

item.title: Prognosis Communication and Caregiver Relationship Are Associated With Return to Acute Care Among Hospitalized Persons With Moderate-to-Severe Dementia
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Return to acute care was common among hospitalized persons with moderate-to-severe dementia and not well explained by patient characteristics alone. Documentation of a dementia prognosis discussion and caregiver relationship were associated with return. These findings identify potentially actionable targets for future dementia-focused palliative and transitional care interventions.

item.title: Impact of the 2017 FDA Drug Safety Communication of Codeine and Tramadol on Pediatric Dental Prescribing in the United States: Evidence of Opioid Prescribing From National Claims Data
item.description: CONCLUSION: The 2017 FDA DSC was associated with reduced pediatric dental codeine prescribing, which was accompanied by an increase in the relative proportion of hydrocodone and oxycodone-involving visits. Drug-specific safety warnings may reduce targeted prescribing without decreasing overall pediatric opioid exposure.

item.title: A Neurobiological Model of Endometriosis-Associated Pain: Stress, Neuroimmune Dysfunction, and Endocannabinoid Signaling
item.description: Endometriosis-associated chronic pelvic pain is a multidimensional pain condition involving persistent peripheral nociceptive input, peripheral and central sensitization, and substantial psychological distress. However, the neurobiological mechanisms linking chronic pain, stress, and affective disturbances remain incompletely understood. This narrative review synthesizes human and preclinical evidence on the interactions among nociceptive processing, neuroimmune signaling, and stress-response...

item.title: The association of nutrition assessment and discharge disposition with 30-day readmission in hospitalized adults with a medical diagnosis of malnutrition: A retrospective study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Inpatient RD-led nutrition assessment with a documented nutrition care plan was independently associated with lower 30-day readmission among malnourished patients. This may reflect improved nutrition care as a result of the RD assessment.

item.title: Itchy Skin-Spinal Sensitization for C-Fibre Input in Healthy Subjects
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Together, these findings demonstrate that spinal itch sensitization extends to C-fibre input and is dynamically maintained by ongoing pruriceptive activity.

item.title: Deuteron beam radiotherapy: A Monte Carlo study relative to protons and helium ions
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Deuterons exhibit properties intermediate between protons and helium ions, with lateral dose characteristics closer to helium and RBE closer to protons. These findings suggest that deuterons may offer a favorable balance between dose conformity, biological effectiveness, and technical complexity, warranting further investigation in clinically realistic settings.

item.title: Effects of Hybrid Closed Loop Automated Insulin Delivery on Time in Tight Range and Hypoglycemic Outcomes Among Older Adults with Type 1 Diabetes: Participant-Level Pooled Analysis from Three Randomized Controlled Trials
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults with T1D, HCL decreases hypoglycemia and increases TITR compared with SAP. Older adults with adequate cognitive and functional capacity can safely achieve better glycemic management with HCL use.

item.title: Spinach-Derived Chlorophyll-Containing Aqueous Extract Attenuates Experimental Colitis: In Vivo Protective and Therapeutic Effects With Molecular Docking Insights
item.description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition of the gastrointestinal tract characterized by sustained inflammation, oxidative stress, and tissue damage. Chlorophyll is a natural green pigment found in plants with reported antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. This study is aimed at evaluating both the preventive and therapeutic effects of a spinach-derived chlorophyll-containing aqueous extract on colitis in rats, supported by molecular docking of key inflammatory targets,...

item.title: Association of Fecal Microbiome Profiles With Hepatic Steatosis and Fatty Pancreas in Adults With Obesity
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Intrahepatic and intrapancreatic fat deposition represents a source of biological variability in gut microbiome studies in obesity. MRI-based ectopic fat phenotyping may improve stratification and biological interpretation in microbiome studies of obesity-related metabolic dysfunction.

item.title: Impulsivity and Alcohol Use in Young Adults: An EMA Study on Momentary Antecedents
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Momentary within-person impulsivity predicted reductions in concurrent AC in a clinical AUD sample, challenging dominant theoretical frameworks. Findings highlight the importance of temporal dynamics, social context, and self-medication processes in understanding impulsivity-alcohol associations in everyday life.

item.title: Optimal Timing to Initiate Conversion Surgery for Initially Unresectable Gastric Cancer: A Retrospective Multicenter Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Initiating conversion surgery at 4.5-6.0 months (5~6 cycles) might optimize survival and tumor response without increasing surgical risks in unresectable gastric cancer.

item.title: Xeno-Free Peptide-Functionalized Hydrogels Support hiPSC Encapsulation and In Situ Differentiation Into Cardiomyocytes With Enhanced Structural Maturation
item.description: While defined synthetic substrates can replace Matrigel for human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) culture and hiPSC-derived cardiomyocyte (hiPSC-CM) production, existing approaches culture cells on two-dimensional surfaces and yield structurally immature cardiomyocytes, limiting their use in disease modeling and regenerative medicine. Here, we developed a xeno-free, fully defined cyclic RGD (cRGD)-functionalized alginate platform in which we encapsulated hiPSCs to support their expansion...

item.title: Health information-seeking behavior among older adults with oral frailty: a latent profile analysis and associated factors
item.description: CONCLUSION: HISB was heterogeneous among hospital-recruited older dental outpatients with oral frailty. These observational findings suggest that eHealth literacy, social support, oral health behaviors, and healthcare access may be relevant targets for future prospective intervention studies.

item.title: Chemical Labeling Identifies Doubly Electrophilic Anti-Inflammatory Manumycin-Type Natural Product U-62162 and a Novel O-Acetylated Derivative
item.description: Manumycin-type natural products exhibit diverse bioactivities, but their immunomodulatory potential remains underexplored. Here, we identified the known metabolite U-62162 A and a previously undescribed C-4 O-acetylated analog, U-62162 B, from the Czech forest soil isolate Streptomyces sp. BCCO 10_1500. Electrophilic metabolites were labeled directly in crude extract using a cysteine-based thiol probe and prioritized by MS/MS molecular networking through a diagnostic reporter ion, enabling rapid...

item.title: Association of dupilumab treatment with incident vitiligo and alopecia areata in atopic dermatitis
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Understanding implementation patterns of the FICUS family support intervention: a matrixed multiple case study across Swiss adult intensive care units
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Implementation success of the FSI across ICUs was moderate to high. Contextual determinants were largely similar across sites. No distinct determinant configurations explaining implementation success were identified, likely due to shared challenges, the small number of sites and the limited sample size.

item.title: Extended Intervention for Tobacco Use (EXIT) for people experiencing homelessness: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
item.description: BACKGROUND: Approximately 70% of people experiencing homelessness smoke cigarettes, compared to 9.9% in the US general population. Barriers to quitting and sustaining cessation include structural inequities (e.g., lack of housing; limited treatment access), and high rates of serious mental illness and substance use disorders. Existing cessation treatments are often brief, not integrated into community service settings, and lack ongoing behavioral support. Community pharmacies represent a...

item.title: Global variability in cardiovascular care of pediatric cancer patients and survivors: survey results from the International Cardio Oncology Society (ICOS)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This global survey highlights an urgent need for standardized cohesive, global, standardized approaches to cardiovascular management in CCS. This study reveals significant variability in cardiovascular risk discussions, screening, and HF management for CCS, with differences by specialty and resource setting.

item.title: Open-source DNA-encoded library informatics package for design, decoding, and analysis: DELi
item.description: BACKGROUND: DNA-encoded library (DEL) technology has become a powerful tool in modern drug discovery. However, fully harnessing its potential requires the use of extensive computational methods, which are often available only through proprietary software. This restricts accessibility for small teams lacking robust informatics support, hindering the growth of the technology.

item.title: Preparation and epitope mapping of broad-spectrum neutralizing antibodies targeting the S2 subunit of the porcine epidemic diarrhea virus spike protein
item.description: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) is a major enteric pathogen of swine, causing severe diarrhea and high mortality in neonatal piglets. The spike (S) protein mediates viral entry, and its conserved S2 subunit, which is responsible for membrane fusion, represents a promising target for broad-spectrum neutralization. However, the antigenic architecture of the PEDV S2 subunit remains poorly defined. In this study, we expressed the recombinant PEDV S2 protein in a baculovirus system. The...

item.title: The effects of affective expectations on affective experience and dimensions of anhedonia in inpatients with major depressive disorder: a randomized clinical trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: Inducing positive expectations in modifying affective experiences and anhedonia-related features can be considered as a promising therapeutic approach in anhedonia treatment.

item.title: Development and preliminary evaluation of a short web-based home multimodal prehabilitation program for patients undergoing major surgery: a single-arm clinical trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective single-arm study, participation in a short web-based home multimodal prehabilitation program was associated with an improvement in preoperative 6MWD. Greater adherence was correlated with greater improvement in 6MWD.

item.title: Interplay of neuropeptide Y, metabolic dysfunction, and inflammation in cognitive impairment of major depressive disorder: a sex-stratified study
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study reveals a sex-specific pathway linking NPY, metabolic dysfunction, and inflammation to cognitive decline in MDD. The integrated biomarker panel offers superior diagnostic utility. Longitudinal studies are warranted for causality and intervention potential.

item.title: Cyberknife® stereotactic radiotherapy versus hippocampus-sparing whole brain radiotherapy with boost in patients with multiple brain metastases-the CyberChallenge trial (ARO v-2021-05): a study protocol for a prospective, open-label, randomized, two-arm, phase II study
item.description: BACKGROUND: Patients suffering from malignancies in advanced stages often develop brain metastases, which limit both the life span and quality of life. Most innovative treatment options are single or multifraction stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) and hippocampus-sparing whole brain radiotherapy with simultaneously integrated boost to large metastases (HS-WBRT ± SIB) as they are suspected to be beneficial regarding toxicity without compromising efficacy. However, especially in the patient cohort...

item.title: Multi-target hypoglycemic agents in glucose metabolism disorders and neurodegenerative diseases
item.description: Glucose metabolism disorders (GMDs) are a major global health challenge, characterized by overlapping pathophysiological mechanisms. Emerging research has illuminated a reciprocal association between diabetes mellitus (DM) and neurodegenerative diseases (NDs). Specifically, hyperglycemic states intensify neuroinflammatory cascades, oxidative stress, and aberrant protein misfolding (e.g. amyloid-β aggregation), whereas neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) disrupt systemic glucose homeostasis.Thus,...

item.title: Distinct contributions of AXL and CD274 to the maintenance of acquired radioresistance in melanoma
item.description: Melanoma shows profound resistance to ionizing radiation (IR) and is a major clinical challenge. To identify drivers of acquired radioresistance, we first screened a panel of melanoma cell lines and found that intrinsic radiosensitivity did not correlate with BRAF/NRAS mutations or ALDH^(+) stem cell populations. We then established a radioresistant (RR) subline from the sensitive MelJuso cell line via continuous fractionated irradiation. The resulting MelJuso RR cells exhibited significantly...

item.title: Pathogenesis of lymphangioleiomyomatosis: from TSC mutations, metabolic reprogramming, to microenvironmental interactions
item.description: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis is a rare disease primarily affecting women of reproductive age, characterized by progressive pulmonary cystic destruction and driven by TSC gene loss-induced constitutive mTORC1 activation. Current understanding of the disease extends beyond this primary genetic defect to encompass a multidimensional network involving metabolic reprogramming, tumor microenvironment interactions, and hormonal dependence. This review comprehensively examines the genetic basis and core...

item.title: Synthesis, preclinical evaluation, and the first-in-human study of [<sup>18</sup>F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR for neuroendocrine neoplasms compared with [<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-DOTA-NOC and [<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE
item.description: CONCLUSION: We developed several novel SSTR-targeted probes with favourable physicochemical properties and identified [^(18)F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR as the most promising candidate. Compared with [^(68)Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE and [^(68)Ga]Ga-DOTA-NOC, [^(18)F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR showed superior lesion detection in patients with NENs, supporting its potential for clinical translation.

item.title: Noninvasive retinal features for early prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus: a machine learning-based cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The LIGHT model demonstrates that noninvasive retinal features can enhance early GDM risk stratification, offering a potential complementary approach for prenatal screening.

item.title: Monitoring electronic patient reported outcomes (ePROs) during cancer treatment: protocol for a phased implementation of an ePRO system across seventeen cancer care sites within an integrated healthcare system
item.description: BACKGROUND: Advances in cancer treatment have improved patient survival, but treatment-related toxicities commonly impair patient quality of life and contribute to emergency department visits and hospitalizations. Electronic patient-reported outcomes (ePRO) systems have demonstrated benefits for symptom control, quality of life, and reduced acute healthcare utilization. However, evidence of large-scale implementation within routine oncology care remains limited. We describe a protocol to...

item.title: Private practitioner characteristics and their potential to contribute to tuberculosis management in Indonesia
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PPs have great potential to contribute to TB care because they are present in large numbers, are distributed throughout the city, and can provide services after regular office hours. Some PPs even worked in HCFs supported by X-rays, laboratories, and pharmacies. Ways to engage PPs optimally with the NTP should be sought.

item.title: Chorion status reverses the relative embryotoxicity of bare and sulfidated nanoscale zerovalent iron in zebrafish embryos
item.description: Surface sulfidation is widely used to enhance the remediation performance of nanoscale zerovalent iron (nZVI), yet how the zebrafish chorion shapes developmental toxicity of sulfidated nZVI (S-nZVI) remains unclear. We compared bare nZVI and S-nZVI using complementary guideline-informed chorion-intact and dechorionated zebrafish embryo assays based on OECD Test Guideline 236 and ISO/TS 22082:2020, respectively, with both exposures conducted for 120 h. Although their primary particle sizes were...

item.title: A shared lysosomal and autophagy-related phenotype in human macrophages exposed to low-metallic brake wear PM<sub>2.5</sub> or to the dominant iron oxide constituent
item.description: Braking is a leading non-exhaust source of urban particulate matter, and low-metallic (LM) pads shed debris in which iron oxide is the predominant crystalline phase. Whether that constituent accounts for how the whole wear particle behaves inside a macrophage is unsettled. Differentiated human THP-1 macrophages met LM brake wear PM(2.5) or Fe(2)O(3) over 24 h in serum-free medium at 5 and 50 µg/mL, concentrations leaving viability above 80% of control. Matching on mass left the administered...

item.title: Effect of thermal treatment temperature on the separation behavior of graphite, cathode materials, and lithium from NCM-type black mass
item.description: This study investigated how inert-atmosphere thermal treatment temperature affects the separation behavior of graphite, cathode materials, and lithium in NCM-type black mass. Black mass samples were heat-treated at 400, 500, 600, and 700°C for 2 h under nitrogen and subsequently subjected to flotation, magnetic separation, and water leaching. The results showed that electrolyte- and binder-derived organic species were progressively removed up to 500°C, while cathode materials were reduced up to...

item.title: Repeated-dose toxicity and safety pharmacology of the Ad5/35 adenoviral vector COVID-19 vaccine AdCLD-CoV19-1 LP.8.1 in Sprague-Dawley rats and Beagle dogs
item.description: Ongoing SARS-CoV-2 evolution requires re-matching vaccines to circulating variants. AdCLD-CoV19-1 LP.8.1 is an Ad5/35 chimeric adenovirus vector vaccine encoding the spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 LP.8.1. Because a variant-adapted construct still requires confirmatory safety data, we characterized it under Good Laboratory Practice before clinical testing. Sprague-Dawley rats received three intramuscular doses of 5.0 × 10^(10) viral particles at two-week intervals followed by a four-week recovery...

item.title: Precision readout of a nanoscale single-electron pump using a superconducting current comparator and a quantum Hall resistance array
item.description: Precisely controlled transport and readout of individual electrons are key capabilities for nanoelectronic and quantum devices; however quantitative measurement of their picoampere-scale currents remains a major challenge. Here, we realize a hybrid measurement architecture that couples a gate-defined GaAs/AlGaAs single-electron pump based on a dynamic quantum dot to a high-ratio cryogenic current comparator (CCC) and a quantum Hall resistance (QHR) array. Gate driving of the SEP at 240 MHz...

item.title: Transfer Learning with Graph Neural Networks for Experimental Prediction of Organic Photovoltaic Efficiency
item.description: Herein, we report a transfer learning approach that enhances power conversion efficiency (PCE) predictions in organic photovoltaics (OPVs) by resolving the critical issue of missing descriptors in real-world databases. Specifically, we address the challenge of missing frontier molecular orbital descriptors (HOMO and LUMO) within an extensive data set of 1346 experimental OPV records established by the Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology (KRICT). To resolve this, a graph neural...

item.title: Activity-Guided Development of a Broccoli-Rich Mixed Vegetable Extract: Effects on Cadmium-Associated Oxidative Injury and Tissue Cadmium Concentrations
item.description: Cadmium (Cd) exposure is associated with oxidative injury, highlighting the need to evaluate food-derived preparations with potential protective activity. This study applied activity-guided screening to develop a broccoli-rich mixed vegetable extract (MVE) and investigate its effects in cellular and rat models of Cd exposure. Hot-water extracts of broccoli, tomato, paprika, and grape were first compared in Cd-exposed HepG2 and Vero cells. At 500 μg/mL, broccoli extract exhibited the highest mean...

item.title: A determination of the backscattering probability of low-energy antiprotons
item.description: It is commonly assumed that antiprotons impinging on a material surface annihilate promptly with the nuclei of the material. However, at kinetic energies of a few keV, this assumption may not hold. As with low-energy protons, electrons or positrons that can be reflected from a target, they may undergo large-angle Coulomb scattering before annihilation occurs, thereby appearing to be "backscattered" from the material surface. This backscattering fraction, largely unknown, is a crucial ingredient...

item.title: Hierarchical Chiral Spindle Microbeads for Full-Color Circularly Polarized Luminescence
item.description: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) is a key optical function for chiral photonics, advanced displays, and information security. However, most organic CPL materials rely on intrinsically chiral emitters or fragile chiral supramolecular assemblies, which limits color tunability, structural robustness, and processability. Here, we report hierarchical chiral spindle microbeads (HCSMs) as solid-state chiral templates that convert achiral emitters into full-color CPL media. HCSMs are synthesized...

item.title: Computationally Guided Rational Design of Site-Specific and Serum-Stable Protein-Drug Conjugates for Enhanced Cancer Therapy
item.description: Protein-drug conjugates (PDCs) are an emerging class of biotherapeutics that enable tumor-targeted drug delivery with reduced off-target toxicity. However, conventional maleimide-based conjugation often produces heterogeneous mixtures, resulting in premature drug release and a narrow therapeutic window. Here, we present a computationally assisted cysteine-engineering strategy, termed CYSFOLD, to generate homogeneous, stable PDCs without complex redox procedures or additional chemical...

item.title: Surgical repair of an ostium secundum atrial septal defect with absent dorsal rim in a dog
item.description: CONCLUSION: Surgical closure of a secundum ASD lacking a dorsal rim was successfully achieved using an autologous pericardial patch, resulting in stable defect repair without complications during follow-up.

item.title: Korea10K integrates 10,239 whole genomes with multiomic and clinical health information as a Korean reference dataset
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Korea10K establishes a high-resolution genomic and multiomic reference for the Korean population and reveals a previously unrecognized interaction between genetic variation and epigenomic measurement. This resource provides a foundation for precision medicine and highlights the need for ancestry-aware interpretation of molecular data.
item.category: KAIST, Korea University, POSTECH, Pusan National University, SNU, UNIST

item.title: Integrative multi-omics analyses reveal that exogenous indole-3-lactic acid enhances growth by modulating various metabolic pathways in Lemna aequinoctialis culture
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that ILA can be used to enhance the growth and production of useful metabolites and lipids in L. aequinoctialis as feed, food, and pharmaceutical resources.

item.title: SENNA: hypothesis-driven spatial omics analysis via curve-based coordinate systems
item.description: Current frameworks for spatial omics analysis provide limited support for researchers to design analyses that leverage prior knowledge, such as tissue morphology or visually defined regions with marker overexpression. Here, we present SENNA (Spatial Expression aNalysis with spliNe Axes), a framework that mathematically projects spots onto their closest point on a user-defined curve axis and models continuous spatial variation along the mapped coordinates. Given a curve axis that represents a...

item.title: Genome-wide association analyses of suicidality identify 77 loci and implicate subcortical brain regions and synaptic pathways
item.description: Suicidality contributes substantially to global morbidity and mortality, yet, despite its heritability, its biological etiology remains largely elusive. Here we conducted multi-ancestry genome-wide association study meta-analyses of suicidal ideation (259,747 cases), suicide attempt (64,993 cases), suicide death (9,197 cases) and suicidal behavior (suicide attempt/death, 75,300 cases), across 54 cohorts (for example, the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium, Million Veteran Program and UK Biobank)....

item.title: Functional clustering of cuffless 24-h systolic blood pressure profiles: cohort-derived cut-offs and renal target-organ damage
item.description: Unsupervised analysis of the whole 24-h blood pressure (BP) curve may summarize cuffless recordings differently from the categorical indices developed for cuff-based monitoring. We examined how functional clustering organizes cuffless 24-h systolic BP profiles and whether the groups are associated with renal target-organ damage. We analyzed 1220 Korean adults who underwent cuffless ring-type 24-h ambulatory BP monitoring in 2025. Clock-hour systolic BP was decomposed by functional principal...

item.title: Myosteatosis in muscle aging and metabolic dysfunction: mechanisms, inter-tissue crosstalk, and therapeutic strategies
item.description: Myosteatosis, characterized by pathological fat accumulation within skeletal muscle, has been increasingly recognized as a critical yet often underappreciated factor contributing to muscle quality deterioration, systemic metabolic dysfunction, and overall health decline. Mechanistically, myosteatosis is driven by dysregulated lipid metabolism and mitochondrial dysfunction in concert with chronic low-grade inflammation, leading to muscular fat deposition, insulin resistance, and muscle quality...

item.title: Integrated Proteomic and Network Analysis Reveals Dysregulated Pathways and Proteins in Multiple Myeloma Progression
item.description: Multiple myeloma (MM) remains incurable despite therapeutic advances, reflecting limited understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying disease initiation and progression. MM develops through asymptomatic precursor stages, monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and smouldering multiple myeloma (SMM), before becoming symptomatic. However, studies examining protein-level changes in bone marrow (BM)-derived CD138^(+) plasma cells across the MGUS-SMM-MM continuum remain...

item.title: Trajectories of Cardiovascular and Cancer-Specific Mortality Across Major Cancers in the United States
item.description: CONCLUSION: Cancer-specific mortality exceeded cardiovascular mortality for all eight cancers, but the balance between them varied by cancer type and age. Recent increases in the cardiovascular-to-cancer mortality rate ratio in seven cancers reflected declining cancer-specific mortality and, after 2019, rising cardiovascular mortality; for four cancers they were not evident before 2020 and require continued surveillance.

item.title: Calvarial Cortical Attenuation and Three-Layer Geometry on Routine Computed Tomography: Age- and Sex-Related Associations
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this cross-sectional cohort, calvarial cortical attenuation was lower in older adults, whereas total thickness was not; the association persisted after adjustment for measured cortical-table thickness, but residual partial-volume effects cannot be excluded. Cortical attenuation is a protocol-specific CT descriptor, not bone mineral density, and requires biological and clinical validation.

item.title: Acute Metabolic Responses to High-Intensity Dragon Boat Competition in Elite Female Athletes: A Urine Metabolomics Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: High-intensity dragon boat racing induces acute metabolic reprogramming characterized by enhanced ATP turnover, substantial involvement of the phosphocreatine energy system, and alterations in neurotransmitter-related metabolism.

item.title: GDF-11 attenuates pain without hyperthermia and inhibits TRPV1 channel activity
item.description: Hormonal changes during aging and their association with chronic pain prompted our investigation into the effects of the aging-related growth differentiation factor-11 (GDF-11) on transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) activity. GDF-11 has been reported to relieve neuropathic pain through an action on spinal microglia, but whether it acts on primary sensory neurons, and on TRPV1 in particular, has not been examined. In this study, GDF-11 inhibited capsaicin-evoked calcium responses and...

item.title: Lateral local recurrence after total mesorectal excision alone in rectal cancer with radiologically responsive lateral pelvic nodes: incidence and associated factors in the RESPONDER-TME study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Isolated LLR was uncommon after TME alone in selected patients with radiologically responsive LPNs, suggesting favorable lateral control following omission of LPND in this cohort. BMI <23 kg/m² and pre-nCRT CEA ≥5 ng/mL were associated with isolated LLR in exploratory analyses, requiring further validation before clinical application.

item.title: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy-based computer-aided diagnosis of major depressive disorder: A meta-classification approach integrating multiple task-specific classifiers
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Integrating task-specific classifiers derived from distinct cognitive tasks improved classification performance, supporting the value of combining complementary diagnostic information across tasks. These findings underscore the potential of multi-task fNIRS for improving the reliability of CAD of MDD.
item.category: Hanyang University, Pusan National University, SNU

item.title: Orthosomnia and consumer sleep technologies: A narrative review and industry-academia perspective of risk factors, safeguards, and technology design recommendations
item.description: Sleep tracking is among the most widely adopted consumer health-monitoring behaviors, yet growing evidence suggests it can become counterproductive for a vulnerable subset of users. Orthosomnia-a preoccupation with achieving perfect or 'correct' sleep, for which recurrent consumer sleep technology (CST) use is the most commonly reported risk factor-has gained clinical attention but lacks a consensus definition, validated prevalence data, and evidence-based management guidance. item.title: Small-molecule targeting of CMTM6 induces dual degradation of PD-L1 and SLC1A5 to enhance cancer immunotherapy
item.description: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized oncology; however, emerging therapeutic resistance and the pharmacokinetic limitations of monoclonal antibodies necessitate the development of potent, small-molecule alternatives. CMTM6 (CKLF-like MARVEL transmembrane domain-containing protein 6) has recently been identified as a master posttranslational regulator of PD-L1 stability. item.title: Comparison of Anterograde, Retrograde, and Extracapsular Dissection in Benign Parotid Surgery: A Network Meta-Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: EC was associated with substantially reduced risks of facial nerve palsy and other postoperative morbidities compared with AG, whereas RG did not confer statistically significant advantages. These findings support EC as a favorable surgical approach for benign parotid tumors; however, further high-quality randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm these results.

item.title: Skin temperature changes after thoracic sympathetic block: a large retrospective analysis of optimal measurement sites
item.description: CONCLUSION: A distal-to-proximal temperature gradient was evident, with the palm and dorsum of the hand best reflecting the physiological effect of TSB. These findings support the use of distal regions for assessing the physiological effect of sympathetic blockade in the upper extremity.

item.title: Minimally invasive resection of adrenal neuroblastoma including high-risk disease: a propensity score-matched two-center analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: MIS for adrenal neuroblastoma, including stage M disease, shortened hospital stay without a detectable difference in overall survival. The higher recurrence with the centers pooled is best read as an upper bound; most recurrences were distant. MIS was applied almost exclusively to IDRF-negative tumors, beyond which the data define no selection criteria.

item.title: Changing gastric cancer epidemiology in the U.S.: age-specific patterns in stage at diagnosis and treatment by race/ethnicity and Asian subgroup
item.description: CONCLUSION: The proportion of localized- and distant-stage gastric cancer among patients increased over two decades. Younger patients were more often present with advanced disease, whereas older patients had higher rates of non-treatment despite localized tumors.

item.title: Richardson-type metabolic pattern predicts clinical progression in progressive supranuclear palsy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The (richardson)PSPRP expression may be useful for assessing disease burden across the PSP spectrum, warranting validation in large multicenter cohorts.

item.description: Designing polymer binders that simultaneously regulate mechanical stability and electronic/ionic transport remains a critical challenge for high-performance silicon (Si) anodes.
